title: The data directory, tablespaces and where the files really live

videos.script: Ask a developer where their data is and they will name a database. Ask the operating system and it will name a directory. {{directory}} Both are right, and this lesson is the bridge between them. A table you created with one statement is, on disk, a handful of files with numbers for names. {{numbers}} You will load a database of a million orders and then go and find it. Which directory holds it. Which file is the orders table. Why there are three files and not one. {{three}} Then you will move a table to another disk, and watch PostgreSQL leave a symbolic link behind to remember where it went. {{tablespace}} And you will learn the short list of things in that directory nobody touches by hand. Every one of them has destroyed a database somewhere, for somebody who thought they were tidying up. {{hands-off}} Knowing where the files are is what lets you answer the questions that come later. How much space a table really takes. What fills a disk. What a backup has to copy. {{title}}
